## Flex Wins 2026 Automotive News PACE Award for Fully Symmetric HV DC/DC Architecture


November 20, 2026


- High Voltage (HV) DC/DC Converter named a 2026 PACE Award winner, recognizing its innovative Dual Active Bridge architecture that enables fully symmetric, isolated power transfer with fast dynamic response and a wide operating range
- Technology helps automakers simplify vehicle electrical architectures, improve power management, and minimize reliance on auxiliary low-voltage energy storage
- Solution lowers system complexity, enables weight and cost savings, and enhances reliability


AUSTIN, Texas


, Nov. 20, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Flex (NASDAQ: FLEX) today announced that its HV DC/DC Converter has been named a[2026 Automotive News PACE Award winner](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4828057-1&h=4179759472&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.autonews.com%2Fmanufacturing%2Fsuppliers%2Fan-pace-awards-pace-pilot-innovation-list-2026%2F&a=2026+Automotive+News+PACE+Award+winner) , recognizing its innovative approach to high-voltage power conversion designed for the evolving electrical demands of electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles.


As vehicle architectures become more electrified and software-defined, automakers face growing demands on the systems that power safety-critical and high-performance electrical functions. The Flex HV DC/DC Converter addresses these challenges with a scalable, bidirectional architecture that supports both 400V and 800V traction battery systems and responds quickly to dynamic vehicle loads.


"Winning a third PACE Award in two years is an honor and a testament to Flex's continued innovation in automotive power and compute," said Andreas Heim, Vice President of Automotive at Flex. "This latest recognition highlights our expanding capabilities across both high- and low-voltage power systems as automakers move toward increasingly sophisticated electrified vehicle architectures."


The DC/DC platform uses a dual active bridge-based architecture to provide wide input-voltage capability and bidirectional energy flow. By responding dynamically to changing electrical demands, it can help automakers simplify electrical architectures, reduce reliance on auxiliary low-voltage energy storage, and improve system reliability. It also supports higher-power applications and integration with onboard chargers, inverters, and software-defined power management.


The award builds on[Flex's 2025 PACE Award](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4828057-1&h=1637426629&u=https%3A%2F%2Finvestors.flex.com%2Fnews%2Fnews-details%2F2025%2FFlex-Wins-Two-2025-PACE-Awards-for-Innovation-in-Automotive-Compute-and-Power-Electronics%2Fdefault.aspx&a=Flex%27s+2025+PACE+Award) for its Backup DC/DC Converter, which provides power continuity for essential drive-by-wire systems. The Automotive News PACE Awards recognize automotive supplier innovations that demonstrate significant technological advancement and business impact, as selected by an independent panel of judges.


Learn more about Flex's automotive HV power electronics solution:[https://flex.com/downloads/high-voltage-power-electronics-system-for-automotive-solution-brief](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4828057-1&h=3994291314&u=https%3A%2F%2Fflex.com%2Fdownloads%2Fhigh-voltage-power-electronics-system-for-automotive-solution-brief&a=https%3A%2F%2Fflex.com%2Fdownloads%2Fhigh-voltage-power-electronics-system-for-automotive-solution-brief)
